Allergies:
scopolamine

Chief Complaint:
Weakness

History of Present Illness:
___ w/ history of severe spinal stenosis on bupivacaine pump and 
Fentanyl patch, HFpEF, permanent AF on Coumadin, CKD III, lung 
CA s/p resection, HNKCC s/p resection, presenting as transfer 
from OSH w/ worsening ___ weakness and s/p fall 1d PTA.

Patient reports that he has felt increasingly weak over the past 
several weeks, primarily in his legs but also in his arms, legs 
greater than arms, left greater than right, resulting in a near 
fall yesterday. Patient reports that he was in the shower, and 
his right leg "gave out", causing him to fall out of his shower 
chair onto the floor, injuring his left ankle. He reports pain 
in
his left ankle and knee. He denies head strike or loss of 
consciousness. No bowel or bladder symptoms. 

He states that he recently had his bupivacaine increased by his 
PCP several weeks ago without improvement in his back pain. 
Subsequently developed worsening weakness as above. 

In ED at ___:
- CT head, cervical spine, lumbar spine showed no acute fracture 
or abnormality.
- BUN increased to 137 well over baseline 
- troponin 0.13
- potassium 2.6
- EKG showed A. fib without ischemic changes. 

In the ED:
- BP 91/49
- Left ankle swollen, moderately tender to palpation, no gross 
deformity, 2+ DP pulse. Left knee also moderately tender to 
palpation, no gross deformity, no overlying sialitis, erythema. 
- spine consulted who thought that there was no indication for a 
surgical intervention. Also stated that although findings are 
likely chronic, if there are still concerns, recommend CT 
myelogram once kidney function is improved and ___ medical 
status has been optimized (Cannot obtain MRI given spine
stimulator).

Of note, the patient gets most of his care at ___. He was last 
hospitalized at ___ in ___ for small volume hemoptysis 
thought to be in the setting of bronchiectasis / PNA and 
completed a 10 day course of Levaquin. Lung CA is in remission.  


10 point ROS performed and otherwise negative.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with history of severe spinal stenosis on bupivacaine pump 
and fentanyl patch, HFpEF, permanent AF on Coumadin, CKD III, 
lung CA s/p LLL segmentectomy, HNKCC s/p resection, COPD, DM2, 
presenting as transfer from ___ with worsening ___ 
weakness and s/p fall 1d prior to admission, found to have coag 
negative staph bactermia.

====================
ACTIVE/ACUTE ISSUES:
====================

# Coag neg staph bacteremia (***VANC LEVELS STILL 
SUPRATHERAPEUTIC -22- ON DAY OF TRANSFER, CHECK VANC LEVEL 
BEFORE INITIATING***)
___ ___ cultures growing coag neg staph in ___ 
bottles. ___ ED ___ cultures also growing coag neg staph in 
___ bottles. Likely genuine bacteremia. Started IV vanc on ___ 
at 1500mg Q12H but was held on ___ given trough returned at 60, 
and have persisted at supratherapeutic levels on daily checks, 
IV vanc still being held. Multiple potential sources/seeding 
sites for coag neg staph. Bilateral knee replacements, L knee 
initially with effusion that resolved in a few days (possibly 
improved with vanc vs diuretics), never had erythema or 
tenderness. Port and PEG sites appear non-infected. Anesthesia 
had low suspicion of intrathecal pump being source given it was 
implanted over ___ year ago and MRI negative for epidural abscess. 
However, pump was recently accessed ___ for cartridge 
change and port accessed around same time for blood draw. 
Laceration on L ankle from fall from shower chair 1 day prior to 
admission does not appear infected, no decubitus ulcers. UA/UCx 
negative. CT torso negative for signs of inflammation/fluid 
collections surrounding hardware. TTE without vegetations. CT 
torso findings reassuring however cannot rule out biofilm 
formation. Following discussion with ID and anesthesia, plan for 
2 week course of vancomycin (___) and trial for eradication 
of bacteremia without hardware removal given patient is poor 
surgical candidate. Recommend administering antibiotics via port 
in case of port associated infection.

# C. diff
On ___ pt developed new leukocytosis, worsened diarrhea, fever, 
and relative hypotension overnight. C. diff PCR positive (stool 
toxin PCR pending) in setting of broad spectrum antibiotic use. 
Started on PO vanc (d1 = ___, plan for ___ on CKD
Unclear baseline creatinine, potentially around 1.4. Creatinine 
initially rose to 1.7 and plateaued, then rose again and has yet 
to peak, was 2.9 on last check. Urine spun, consistent with ATN, 
likely from 2 separate insults, suspect CIN (from CT torso as 
above) and vanc nephropathy given vanc levels over 30 for 6 
days. Possible contribution from cardio-renal as suspect patient 
is volume overloaded based on weights (exam challenging as 
below), for which patient has been diuresed aggressively with 
furosemide drip. On day of transfer Cr peaked at 3.0 and 
downtrended to 2.7 on pm lytes with continued diuresis with 
Lasix gtt at 20.

# Lower abdominal pain, likely obstructed foley
Started having lower abdominal pain night of ___, am 
examination on ___ significant for suprapubic tenderness with 
moderate palpation, as well as LLQ and RLQ tenderness with deep 
palpation. Bladder scan showed 775cc despite foley, foley 
exchanged and pain much improved.

# Symptomatic uremia
BUN persistently elevated above 100 since admission, out of 
proportion to creatinine, with symptomatic myoclonus and 
myopathy. On TFs, no excessive protein intake. Hgb stable. 
Unclear etiology. Nephrology consulted and suspect from HF with 
poor effective circulating volume. Volume exam difficult as 
below. ___ have worsened with holding diuresis and 1L fluid 
challenge (vs ATN running its course). Remained stable during 
active diuresis, continuing active diuresis as above.

# HFpEF exacerbation
Per ___ records dry weight ~ 211 lbs (per wife has been as low 
as 199 lbs), BNP ~ 5k. Likely triggered by infection as above vs 
increased free water flushes in tube feeds for prior 
hypernatremia. Shortly after admission developed new O2 
requirement as above, diffuse pulmonary edema seen on initial 
CXR (in addition to showing pneumonia as above), proBNP elevated 
to ___. TTE redemonstrating normal EF, diastolic dysfunction. 
Elevated left sided filling pressures concerning for true volume 
overload. Underwent active diuresis with Lasix gtt at 10 with 
significant improvement in respiratory status the next day even 
though bed weights continued to increase (consistent with I/Os, 
getting a lot of fluid in tube feeds). Ongoing volume assessment 
has been a challenge. Bed weights seem reliable as progressively 
increased from 211 on admission to 240s over the course of 12 
days with consistent trend and have been consistent with I/Os. 
Exam however is challenging as patient is without 
___ edema, has JVP elevated >15cm but also has 
TR and pulmonary HTN. Suspect he may be accumulating in his 
abdomen. At one point was concerned about possible volume down 
given persistent uremia, ___, and lack of edema on exam, however 
holding diuretics and giving 1L fluid challenge may have 
worsened rather than improved kidney function as above 
(difficult to say for sure given concurrent ATN running its 
course), while kidney function seemed to at least remain stable 
during active diuresis for 4 days and then the 3 days leading up 
to transfer. Repeat CT following the first 4 days of active 
diuresis showed stable L sided effusion and not much evidence of 
pulmonary edema, though a conversation with his cardiologist at 
___, Dr. ___ his ventricular dysfunction has a 
significant right-sided component. Restarted furosemide drip at 
20mg/hr on ___ given suspicion for true volume overload from 
right sided failure.

# Permanent AF. CHADS2=3
On WA and propranolol at home. WA initially held given potential 
proceduralization, was restarted with daily redosing following 
finalization of treatment plan for infection as above. Started 
heparin bridge despite CHADS2 score of 3 because CT torso showed 
possible left atrial thrombus. TTE negative for atrial thrombus, 
but wasn't a dedicated study for thrombus so can't completely 
rule out. Remains on heparin gtt and daily dosing of warfarin.

# Hyponatremia
# Hypernatremia (resolved)
Na increased to 150s a couple days after admission, tube feed 
free water flushes increased to 400cc Q4H and since then Na 
remained stable in ___ for a few days, started downtrending 
and developed mild hyponatremia to low 130s, decreased tube feed 
free water flushes to 200cc Q4H on day of transfer.

# ___ weakness
# Severe spinal stenosis
Seen by spine in the ED and found to have no indication for 
urgent surgical intervention. Rectal tone in ED normal, no 
saddle anesthesia. However, did have urinary retention (which 
could, however, be confounded by opioid use). Developed new 
worsening of lower extremity weakness L>R the day after 
admission, may have been confounded by pain but in combination 
with urinary retention, c/f cord compression. MRI showed likely 
cauda equina compression but secondary to chronic changes. 
Surgery indicated but not emergent. Patient is also poor 
surgical candidate given comorbidities and per his wife, ___ 
providers have told them he cannot be intubated due to an airway 
the "size of a straw" as a sequelae of his past operation for 
his posterior hypopharyngeal wall squamous cell carcinoma. For 
the time being, focus on treating infections as above and 
readdress afterwards.

# ___ acquired pneumonia
Two days after admission developed fever, SOB, cough, new O2 
requirement, and CT with bilateral consolidations c/w HAP. MRSA 
screen negative (though still "on" vanc as above), completed 7 
day course of cefepime. Follow up CT scan showed dramatic 
improvement of RLL consolidation, L sided consolidation stable.

# Left Pleural effusion
Likely chronic in association with history of LLL segmentectomy 
for his previous lung cancer and heart failure. IP was 
consulted, given concern that active diuresis was not affecting 
effusion; they performed an ultrasound but a sufficient amount 
of fluid was available to be tapped.

# Hyperglycemia
# Type II DM
Insulin requirements likely elevated iso infection. Hx DM2 but 
not on oral anti-hyperglycemics or insulin at home. Started 
glargine QHS and adjusted based on fingersticks, currently at 32 
units given Q6 fingersticks (tube feeds) with ___ units sliding 
scale Humalog/day, resulting in sugars in high 100s to low 200s.

# Nutrition
On bolus tube feeds TID at home. Only allowed ice chips for PO. 
Switched feeds to continuous given not tolerating boluses well 
while in house, and on nepro feeds given ongoing acute on 
chronic kidney injury as above.

# Fall
Occurred 1 day prior to admission as the culmination of his 
progressive weakness. He was sitting in shower chair and fell to 
the left, injury his left shin and ankle. No headstrike or loss 
of consciousness. Trauma workup at ___ negative (x-ray 
left knee/tib-fib/ankle, CT head/c-spine/l-spine).

========================

# HTN
